root_cause.text: In `sound/core/pcm_native.c`'s `snd_pcm_drain()` on linked ALSA PCM streams, a wait-queue entry was initialized with `init_waitqueue_entry()` and conditionally removed only if the target substream was still in the group, so a concurrent UNLINK could leave the entry queued on an old `sleep` list and then re-add it to a new one, corrupting the wait-queue lists.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says `init_waitqueue_entry` “does not clear entry.prev/next” and the “conditional remove_wait_queue ... is skipped when to_check is no longer in the group after concurrent UNLINK,” leaving an orphaned wait entry that later gets added to another queue; the fix replaces this with `init_wait_entry()/prepare_to_wait()/finish_wait`, where `init_wait_entry` clears `prev/next` and `finish_wait` handles removal safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update snd_pcm_drain() to use prepare_to_wait() for interruptible wait-queue setup instead of the older manual sequence.
intent_record.what: In snd_pcm_drain(), the code that sets up waiting on to_check->sleep was changed from using init_waitqueue_entry(), set_current_state(TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE), and add_wait_queue() to using init_wait_entry() and prepare_to_wait(..., TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE).
intent_record.how: This changes the wait-queue setup to the newer wait preparation API, which both initializes the wait entry and puts the task into the interruptible wait state in a single step before releasing the IRQ lock and sleeping. Runtime behavior remains a blocking drain wait, but the wait handling is now done through the proper helper sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use finish_wait() instead of remove_wait_queue() to correctly complete wait-queue cleanup in snd_pcm_drain().
intent_record.what: In the loop inside snd_pcm_drain(), the code changed the cleanup call from remove_wait_queue(&to_check->sleep, &wait) to finish_wait(&to_check->sleep, &wait) when s->runtime matches to_check.
intent_record.how: This changes wait-queue teardown from a raw queue removal to the full wait-completion helper, which properly finalizes the waiter state before exiting the loop and avoids leaving the task in an inconsistent wait condition.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly modifies snd_pcm_drain() wait-queue handling, replacing the manual init_waitqueue_entry()/add/remove pattern with prepare_to_wait(), which is the area implicated by the linked-stream UNLINK race and wait-queue corruption.

The change directly matches the described root cause in snd_pcm_drain(): improper wait-queue entry cleanup during linked PCM stream draining. Replacing remove_wait_queue() with finish_wait() addresses the stale queued entry / list corruption issue caused by concurrent UNLINK.

candidates.rationale: This manually initializes a wait-queue entry before the sleep list is safely managed. In the vulnerable sequence, the entry can remain associated with an old wait queue across a concurrent UNLINK, enabling it to be re-added incorrectly and corrupt the wait-queue lists.

This adds the wait-queue entry to the substream's sleep list in the old manual wait setup. Because the cleanup was conditional on the stream still being in the group, a concurrent UNLINK could leave the entry on the old list and later re-add it, which is the corruption trigger.

This cleanup was only performed when a matching substream was still found in the group. If UNLINK happened concurrently, the wait entry might not be removed at all, leaving stale linkage on the old sleep queue and causing list corruption when reused.

vuln_statements.explanation: This manually initializes the wait-queue entry in the old drain wait sequence. In the vulnerable flow, the entry could remain linked to an old sleep queue across a concurrent UNLINK, setting up later corruption when the same entry was re-added.

This adds the wait-queue entry to the substream sleep list using the old manual pattern. Because cleanup was conditional on the stream still being in the group, a concurrent UNLINK could leave the entry on the old list and then allow it to be added again, corrupting the wait-queue lists.

This cleanup was only executed when a matching substream was still present. If a concurrent UNLINK occurred, the wait entry might not be removed from the old sleep queue, leaving stale linkage that later caused list corruption.

Author: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

    ALSA: pcm - Simplify snd_pcm_drain() implementation
    
    Simplify snd_pcm_drain() implementation and avoid unneeded array-
    allocation for waitqueues.  Instead, one waitqueue is used for the
    first draining stream, and wait until all streams finished.
    
    Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

diff --git a/sound/core/pcm_native.c b/sound/core/pcm_n
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this version. The old code that used per-stream wait-queue records and only removed them later is gone: the diff deletes `struct drain_rec`, the `kmalloc(substream->group->count * sizeof(*drec), GFP_KERNEL)` allocation, `init_waitqueue_entry(&d->wait, current)`, and the delayed cleanup loop over `remove_wait_queue(&runtime->sleep, &d->wait)`. Instead, the code now uses a single local `wait_queue_t wait;` and, crucially, for each iteration it does `init_waitqueue_entry(&wait, current); add_wait_queue(&to_check->sleep, &wait); ... up_read(&snd_pcm_link_rwsem); ... down_read(&snd_pcm_link_rwsem); ... remove_wait_queue(&to_check->sleep, &wait);`. This means the wait entry is explicitly removed after each sleep cycle, so the old stale-queue / re-add-on-new-list corruption scenario is already addressed here.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is in snd_pcm_drain(): a wait-queue entry is added to a target substream's sleep queue, and on wakeup it is removed unconditionally only for the originally chosen queue. In this commit, that logic has been changed. The snippet shows the old global link read-lock usage removed and replaced with a re-check under group ref/lock: after waking, it does `snd_pcm_stream_lock_irq(substream); group = snd_pcm_stream_group_ref(substream); snd_pcm_group_for_each_entry(s, substream) { if (s->runtime == to_check) { remove_wait_queue(&to_check->sleep, &wait); break; } } snd_pcm_group_unref(group, substream);`. This explicitly verifies the substream is still in the relevant group before removing the wait entry, preventing the stale-queue/re-add corruption. The earlier vulnerable pattern of blindly removing the wait queue without re-validating group membership is no longer present in this function body, so has_bug=false and is_fixed=true.
